item.content:encoded:
I'm always delighted to see people trying interesting and new ways to tell stories here. The writing could use some improvement, but it does its job, and the art is compelling and expressive.

I admit that the non-human nature of Dr. Whitney threw me for a loop at first, but I think you made the right call by not addressing it - it became clear a few panels in that their appearance wasn't anything special to the characters, so I just accepted it at that point.*

I also very much appreciate how that non-human nature didn't feel gratuitous at all, but was very much a part of the fabric of the story. This wouldn't have worked nearly as well if Dr. Whitney were human.

I know a lot of other people here take issue with that weirdness aspect, but honestly, you handled that part remarkably well. <3

Definite +1 from me.

* full disclosure: I'm a filthy xenophile so I'm all for seeing more monster/alien critters haha

item.content:encoded:
I gotta somewhat second sirpudding on this, although my main problem with this lies in a different aspect. The art is nice, but the presented story and the presentation itself lack any depth or interesting details whatsoever. The characters' dialogue isn't believable and the way they interact at times feels as if it's a comedic story, which doesn't connect well with the supposedly serious dramatic moment the tale is trying to achieve (and using antropomorphic lizard as a researcher doesn't help here either).

The story and characters are only used to present a pretty blunt and simplistic dilemma (whether should take revenge or act professionally) which is more about the character's own personal demons and inability to fight them off than about being morally right/wrong. The story didn't provide much development for the character itself or the person they've decided to murder, so the drama, for the most part, falls flat.

As I said, I really dig the visual part. But since it's a writing site, I see the writing itself as the most crucial part of a tale, even if it's done in such an unusual format. I don't think anything here besides the art was that good, and for that reason it's a downvote from me.

I hope you enjoy this little project of mine. I have spent the last few months working on this and I think I am happy with the final product. This started as only 4 pages and is around 15 wow. This is honestly the first comic I have finished since I don't count my first post which was only a page long.

For this idea, I wanted to explore the idea of justice and create a situation where there is no easy answer. I didn't want to tell the reader what was right or wrong I wanted you to decide and I hope I accomplished that.

Thank you Alces_alces, Magic8Ball04, AnActualCrow , cybersqyd, Sonderance, Dr Remember, Einer von Rabe, Luvview, and anyone else who I may be forgetting.
